title: Space is discrete below the scales probed by experiment

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Space is discrete below the scales probed by experiment

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Space, though experimentally continuous down to about 10^-20 meters, is very likely made of discrete elements at still smaller scales, just as fluids and other seemingly continuous things have turned out to be.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Particle physics experiments have shown that space acts as a continuum down to distances of around 10^(-20) meters—or a hundred thousandth the radius of a proton. But there is absolutely no reason to think that discrete elements will not be found at still smaller distances.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “The Nature of Space” (from p. 472), p. 472. Scope: the structure of physical space at very small distances

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-12: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The hypothesis has measurable consequences in specified models, and current data impose indirect constraints. Existing resolution does not reach the claimed scale, so direct resolution requires new observations or experiments.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test high-energy and precision observations for violations of continuous spacetime predictions, such as modified dispersion, anisotropy, or a minimum resolvable length. A reproducible discreteness-specific signature would support the claim, while increasingly stringent null results would constrain but not prove continuity.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Available experiments are far above the proposed microscopic scale.

Null results cannot exclude discreteness at all smaller scales.

Different discrete models predict different observable signatures.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.78
discriminating power: 0.68
data adequacy: 0.18

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Collider compilations can reconfirm that space behaves as a continuum down to roughly the scale Wolfram names. That reconfirmation does not discriminate discreteness at still smaller distances from a continuum at all scales. The positive claim needs shorter-distance data that have not been collected.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare scattering and other short-distance probes with a continuum cross-section down to a stated length, and look for a breakdown that a discrete substrate would produce below about 10^-20 m. Continuum behavior at all accessible scales leaves the discreteness claim untouched; a scale-dependent deviation fitted by a discrete cutoff would support it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Present null results are what the claim predicts, since it places discreteness below the probed scale.

No public dataset reaches the distances at which discrete elements are asserted to exist.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.62
analysis feasibility: 0.52
discriminating power: 0.28
data adequacy: 0.24
